title: How this project runs, and where findings about it belong
body:
## Note

This is the anchor for records about the project itself rather than about the
mathematics. If you have learned something about how the collaboration works -- a way of
running it that fails, a piece of the tooling that misleads, a convention that turns out
not to survive contact with people -- it belongs in a record linked to this one.

The corpus therefore has two parts that are not joined to each other: the mathematics,
and this. That is deliberate. A finding about the machinery has no natural place in a
graph of questions about stable commutator length, and forcing a link to one would be
false. What it needs instead is somewhere of its own to hang, so that it is findable by
somebody who is looking for it and does not simply sit unattached.

Why keep such records at all, rather than putting them in a wiki or an email thread. Two
reasons, and the first is the weaker one: the machinery is part of what is being tried
here, and the experiment is not only mathematical. The second matters more. A corpus that
records only theorems teaches its members, by example and without ever saying so, that
everything else is not worth writing down -- including the dead ends in how the work is
organised, which are exactly as expensive to rediscover as mathematical ones and rather
more embarrassing to repeat.

What belongs here:

- how the tooling fails, and what was tried before discovering it
- conventions that were adopted and then had to change, and why
- the record vocabulary itself, which has already changed more than once in response to
  real content and will change again
- decisions about how the project is hosted, governed and credited, where the reasoning
  would otherwise be lost
- anything learned about working with AI assistants on mathematics, which is a large part
  of the point of the exercise and about which almost nothing is established

What does not belong here: the mathematics, which has its own goals to hang from; and
grumbling, which is not a finding.

One caution. These records are subject to exactly the same rules as the rest of the
corpus. They are public and permanent, they carry your name, and they cannot be retracted.
A finding about a person is not a finding about the project.
